key_insight: The paper introduces a “living” benchmark that can automatically generate and refresh evaluation questions for information retrieval from electronic health records. This makes it easier to test LLM-based clinical assistants as medical records, workflows, and models evolve.
problem_solved: Traditional EHR benchmarks are expensive to create by hand, hard to maintain, and quickly become outdated as clinical data and AI systems change. The paper addresses the need for a scalable, up-to-date way to evaluate information retrieval from patient records.
method: Automatically generates question–answer pairs from longitudinal EHR data.
Designs a benchmark framework that can be updated continuously as new records and clinical patterns appear.
Provides a scalable evaluation pipeline for testing LLM-based clinical assistants on information retrieval tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to evaluate clinical assistants more safely and consistently over time. It helps reduce benchmark drift and supports more reliable deployment of LLMs in healthcare settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing EHR data flowing into automated QA generation and benchmark updates.
Side-by-side comparison of static manual benchmarks vs. the living benchmark approach.
Example patient timeline with highlighted information retrieval questions.
Icon set showing scalability, freshness, and clinical safety.
paper_title: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records
paper_authors: Jordan L. Cahoon, Chloe O. Stanwyck, Sulaiman Somani, Philip Chung, Kevin R Keet
